findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple dead adult roaches on the floor in dry storage. PIC stated the Pest Control Log is in the main office. Advise updating log for Pest Control Provider. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned in their entirety to better monitor pest activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment:
Facility does not have sufficient hot water available at the 3 compartment sink to meet demand throughout operation. Staff indicated that hot water is available in the morning. However by lunchtime, staff are heating pots of water on the stove to use while washing dishes. Ensure sufficient hot water is available to meet need.
5-103.11: The water source and system shall be of sufficient capacity to meet the peak water demands (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Food employee observed turning the faucet off with bare hands after washing hands. CORRECTED- Discussed handwashing procedure with employee and PIC. Employees must use a barrier (paper towel, for example) to turn faucet off and prevent soiling newly clean hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee portioning canned fruit handled a sanitizer wiping cloth with gloved hands to wipe down the can opener and returned to portioning fruit without a glove change. Proper use of single use gloves was discussed. Employee washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves prior to continuing with the task.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.112 Evidence of roach activity was observed in glue traps with several oriental cockroaches (also known as water bugs) present. Traps were located in the dry storage room, by the freezer along the south wall, and under the 3 part sink along the north wall. Discussed frequency for changing out glue traps. Ensure traps are checked daily and changed as needed (see general comments for additional information).
Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the premises at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee was observed changing gloves without a handwash in between. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks and glove changes. Hands were properly washing prior to putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with food prep. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed prior to putting on gloves and between glove changes.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Plastic container used for storage of food thermometers was soiled with a few small pieces of general debris and buildup. Two of the three thermometers were not in cases allowing for the food contact surfaces to be in direct contact with soiled surfaces. Storage container was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands between ware washing and handling clean pans and parchment paper to begin portioning single service articles for food and was then observed getting ready to put on gloves without first washing hands. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed.

Food employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-501.110 Employee purse was observed on dry storage shelving next to food. Purse was placed in proper storage area behind the storage room door. 

Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - A small amount of sanitizer solution was observed in the third compartment of the 3 part sink. The amount present was not adequate to allow for proper submersion of all items. Manager added more sanitizer solution to allow for proper submersion of all items for 60 seconds prior to setting aside to air dry.
Employee was also observed completing the wash and rinse step all in the first compartment of the 3 part sink. Separation of wash, rinse, and sanitize steps and proper use of all compartments during ware washing process were discussed.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Make sure the sanitizer solution is adequate to allow for full submersion of those items that can be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the 3 part sink.
Educational handout on manual ware washing was provided.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Portions of taco meat and cheese for tacos were observed at 100°F in the warmer. Several bags of taco meat were being hot held above 135°F in a pan of water on the stove until ready for portioning. Manager noted the final cooking temperature was 181°F for taco meat prior to hot holding. Temperature loss occurred during portioning, and manager began to tweak the process so open bags of taco meat that were being portioned from a pan were heated periodically on the stove to maintain the product at proper temperature prior to being placed in the warmer for hot holding. Portions that were below 135°F upon arrival of inspector would be used first; manager did not anticipate there would be any leftovers from lunch today. 

Hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 135°F/above at all times during storage, display, and service.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Jacket and purse were hanging on dry storage shelving upon arrival of inspector. Employee moved belongings to proper storage area.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage areas to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Portions of chili in styrofoam containers in the cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 59F-60F and 61F-65F respectively. Tray was dated 1/10/17 and condensation was observed inside the lids, which prompted concerns related to improper cooling of cooked foods. Manager stated the portions were out of the cooler prior to inspectors' arrival with the intent to reheat the chili. The portions were sitting at ambient temperature for an unknown length of time prior to being placed back in the cooler so the manager could focus on completing another task. Approximately 7 portions of chili were discarded in the trash. Manager was advised to only get foods out for prep when ready to work with said foods (i.e. immediately reheat, etc.). It does not take long for products to get into the temperature danger zone above 41F. 

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41F/below at all times during storage.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. The manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed with the employee.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Always have paper towels ready to dry hands, and use paper towels as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet in order to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands. If more paper towels are needed to finish drying hands once the faucet is shut off, then utilize the already in use paper towels to touch the handle of the dispenser to retrieve fresh paper towels to finish drying hands.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Wet wiping cloth was on the prep table and not in use. Wiping cloth was placed back in the sanitizer solution for storage.

Store wet wiping cloths in solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed a bowl of just cooked noodles covered and without a time indicated on the wrapper being stored in the two-door freezer. The noodles were obviously just placed within the freezer. Additional noodles were being boiled on the stove. Pasta salad is being prepared for lunch. Discussed the cooling process with staff members. Make sure that cooling items have a time indicated somewhere. Monitor the cooling of foods to insure benchmarks are met (70F within 2 hours and 40 within six hours). During the inspection, the noodles were uncovered and a papertowel indicatin 9:20am was placed beneath them.  Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food. Food shall be cooled: from 135F to 70F within two hours and from 70F to 41F within four hours. To aide in the cooling process: use multiple shallow pans, store uncovered, place in freezer or quick chiller, and/or use an ice wand or an ice bath.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-820a Observed staff member running large equipment quickly through the sanitizing sink of the 3-part sink. During the inspection, the process was halted and sanitizing was discussed. For baking sheets and large colanders, the equipment will have to be flipped after sixty seconds. Make sure that all other equipment and utensils are allowed to rest fully submerged in solution for at least 60 seconds. For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used. Sanitizing contact time for quaternary ammonia is 60 seconds - immmersed in 200ppm solution.
